summary: POC scoping call to align success criteria, workload sizing, and benchmark plan to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. Customer cares about predictable latency, cost per token, data residency, and auditability. Redwood AE + SE outlined tradeoffs and proposed benchmark plan and timeline.
topics: Success criteria: latency SLOs, percentiles, cost targets, model parity
Workload sizing: QPS, concurrent sessions, average & peak sequence lengths
Benchmarks: synthetic vs recorded traces, tokenization, warm caches, KV cache impact
Deployment decision criteria: security/compliance, cost predictability, burst capacity, data residency
Timeline and next steps for POC and benchmark runs
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Jordan Wells (Redwood SE, joined 15m in), Tom Rivera (Head of ML Ops, Acme), Sarah Lee (CTO), Marcus Dunn (Platform Eng), Leah Kim (Security)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we see Acme's evaluation note and wanted to run through POC scoping, align on success criteria, and then pick a path — hosted, dedicated, or private, yeah.
[00:14] Tom Rivera: Yeah thanks Alex, appreciate it. Quick context from our side: we're exploring options to power an assistant and some summarization pipelines. Latency and cost both matter, and security is non negotiable for some datasets.
[00:25] Sarah Lee: And from exec level, if we go hosted we need clear SLAs and auditability; if we go private, we need a clear timeline and onboarding cost.
[00:35] Priya Kumar: Totally. Quick intro from my side — I'm Priya, I'm the SE, I'll own benchmark design and run. We'll propose a set of tests that match your production mix.
[00:45] Marcus Dunn: Awesome. We have a mix of short-chat queries (avg 30 tokens) and long summarization jobs (avg 1400 tokens), plus some batch embedding workloads. Our 99th percentile latency target for chat is 350 ms, and for summarization we can tolerate higher but want consistent throughput.
[01:05] Priya Kumar: That's really helpful. Can you confirm concurrent sessions and peak QPS?
[01:12] Marcus Dunn: On average 50 concurrent sessions, with peaks up to ~250 QPS during business hours.
[01:20] Alex Chen: Great, so those numbers will guide whether dedicated capacity makes sense — dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; hosted can be cheaper but has more variability at peak unless we reserve burst capacity.
[01:35] Leah Kim: From security, we require SOC2, SSO/SAML, encrypted data at rest with customer-managed KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also, any data leaving our network is restricted; we prefer private or VPC options for regulated datasets.
[01:55] Priya Kumar: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking and on-prem options; we can integrate with KMS/HSM and provide audit logs. For hosted, we have SOC2, SAML SSO, and we can bring KMS in some enterprise plans — but we need to detail the exact control plane boundaries.
[02:15] Sarah Lee: Cost is also a question. For a 3-month POC, we want to compare unit economics — cost per 1k tokens and end-to-end latencies.
[02:25] Alex Chen: We'll prepare a cost model. For Hosted, price is usage-based; Dedicated gives a committed monthly rate (predictable), and Private is generally a license + infra cost. We'll show examples using your QPS and sequence lengths.
[02:40] Tom Rivera: On benchmarks, we want to see cold start behavior, warm-state with KV cache, and async batch vs sync latencies. Also tail latency at 95/99.
[02:50] Priya Kumar: Yep, our benchmark plan will include: (1) replay of your traces to replicate arrival patterns, (2) fixed synthetic sequences to compare raw per-token throughput, (3) KV/prefix caching warmup runs, and (4) failover simulations for hosted fallback scenarios.
[03:10] Jordan Wells: I'll add an A/B test to compare Redwood quantized model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs — e.g., 4-bit vs 8-bit on same architecture to see quality delta.
[03:22] Marcus Dunn: Important that we measure quality too. We'll provide a small eval set with target metrics like ROUGE for summarization and BLEU/semantic similarity for embeddings.
[03:32] Priya Kumar: Good call. We'll run quality checks alongside performance so you can see cost vs quality charts.
[03:40] Sarah Lee: How long for the benchmarks and what environment?
[03:45] Priya Kumar: We recommend a two-week bench window: 3 days to onboard and get traces, 7 days for repeated runs across hosted/dedicated/private where applicable, and final analysis + report in 2 days. For Private we'll need lead time to provision — if on-prem, that's longer.
[04:00] Alex Chen: Timeline example: kickoff this week, get artifacts by Friday, benchmarks the week of Mar 8 (w/c 2026-03-08), and review the week after. Does that align?
[04:12] Tom Rivera: That works; we'll aim to get traces and eval sets by Friday.
[04:18] Leah Kim: A question on data residency: if we use Hosted, can we restrict regionally? We need EU-only for certain customers.
[04:26] Alex Chen: Hosted supports region controls — we have EU regions and can isolate projects; for stricter requirements, Dedicated or Private gives stronger guarantees. We'll document region options in the security pack.
[04:40] Marcus Dunn: On the Dedicated option, how does autoscaling and burst capacity work? We have variable traffic, not constant.
[04:47] Priya Kumar: Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling policies. You can set a baseline reserved capacity with optional burst to shared capacity. That said, bursts to shared capacity may increase variability in tail latency compared to fully private infra.
[05:00] Tom Rivera: And failover? If dedicated goes down in a region, can we automatically fallback to hosted?
[05:07] Alex Chen: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants in hosted or other regions per your policy — but that depends on your tolerance for data leaving the dedicated environment; you'll want to set up policies that control fallback or require manual approval.
[05:20] Sarah Lee: For Private deployment, what's the typical time and lift? We have ops constraints — minimal disruption is key.
[05:27] Priya Kumar: Private (VPC) typically needs ~4-8 weeks including network setup, certs, KMS integration, and validation. On-prem air-gapped deployments take longer. For the POC we can do a lightweight private deployment in a customer VPC to validate functional parity before committing to full on-prem.
[05:45] Jordan Wells: For benchmarking we'll capture metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latencies during peaks, tokens/s per GPU, and cost per 1m tokens for each deployment mode. We'll also log failures and cold start durations.
[05:58] Marcus Dunn: We'll also want tracing to map from our API request down to token generation time so we can identify infra bottlenecks.
[06:06] Priya Kumar: We'll add tracing hooks in the benchmark harness. We'll also provide sample dashboards in Redwood Console to show per-route cost + latency breakdowns.
[06:18] Alex Chen: Next, acceptance criteria for the POC — what would success look like?
[06:24] Tom Rivera: For us: (1) Hosted or Dedicated option meets 99th percentile latency ≤ 600 ms for chat at peak QPS, (2) cost per 1M tokens under $X (we gave a target range offline), (3) KV-cache warmup yields >30% cost savings on summaries, and (4) security checklist satisfied (SOC2, KMS, audit logs).
[06:44] Sarah Lee: And we want a reproducible benchmark report and a recommended deployment decision with cost/risks documented.
[06:50] Alex Chen: We'll capture that in the POC report. For the decision matrix, we'll weigh: security/compliance needs, cost predictability, operational overhead, and performance. Typically: Hosted for lowest setup time and pay-as-you-go; Dedicated when you need predictable throughput and SLAs; Private when you require full control, data residency, or on-prem constraints.
[07:10] Marcus Dunn: Can you provide a sample decision matrix?
[07:13] Alex Chen: Yes — we'll include a matrix that maps your criteria to recommended deployment.
[07:18] Leah Kim: Regarding audit logs and SIEM integration — do you support forwarding logs to our Splunk/Datadog?
[07:24] Priya Kumar: Yes, we can forward audit logs and support log shippers; for Private we can place the control plane inside your VPC for richer log forwarding.
[07:34] Tom Rivera: One practical ask: can Redwood run a short synthetic benchmark now so we have a baseline number before providing our traces?
[07:41] Priya Kumar: We can run a quick synthetic test against a representative open model and share rough tokens/sec numbers within 48 hours; however those won't reflect your tokenization patterns or mix.
[07:52] Alex Chen: We'll do that and send it as a baseline.
[07:56] Jordan Wells: Also, we'll include recommendations on model variants and quantization that preserve quality while cutting cost — and propose guardrails for automatic fallback if quality drops.
[08:07] Sarah Lee: On evaluation of quality, will the POC include human-in-loop checks?
[08:11] Priya Kumar: We can include a small human review set, or you can run automated metrics; we'll suggest both.
[08:18] Tom Rivera: Ok good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:21] Alex Chen: We just need the traces, a list of sample prompts for each workload, and the eval set. We'll draft the benchmark plan and cost model and send later today.
[08:30] Marcus Dunn: We'll circulate traces and evals by Friday.
[08:35] Leah Kim: I'll confirm exact KMS/HSM requirements and whether we need an on-prem only solution.
[08:40] Alex Chen: Great. Recap of action items...
[08:45] Alex Chen: Alex will send pricing + SLA options and cost model. Priya will share benchmark plan. Marcus will share traces. Leah will confirm KMS. We'll target bench kickoff w/c 2026-03-08 and a review around Mar 18.
[09:02] Sarah Lee: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:06] Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the benchmark docs.

Optional notes:
- Shared artifacts referenced: benchmark-plan-template.xlsx (will be shared), security-pack.pdf (SOC2/ISO snippets), cost-model-example.csv
- Quality of transcript: medium — some names and acronyms may be slightly off

End of transcript.
